results.name: Citrix NetScaler CVE-2026-88771: Observed Exploitation Artifacts and Hunt Indicators
results.description: CVE-2026-88771 is a critical pre-authentication command-injection vulnerability affecting Citrix NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway. LevelBlue's Threat Hunt Operations & Research (THOR) team identified active exploitation across multiple customer environments featuring malicious authentication events with attacker-controlled usernames containing pitboss and NSPPE strings. Observed activities included command-execution testing, payload retrieval using curl and wget, configuration collection and staging, reverse-shell deployment, persistence mechanisms, web-shell installation, and attempted exfiltration of NetScaler configuration data. Analysis revealed two second-stage payloads: main.py establishing reverse shells to command-and-control infrastructure, and update_c08937.pl creating privileged accounts, deploying PHP web shells, and attempting configuration exfiltration. results.name: PaperCut MF Zero-Day Intrusion: Java Loader, Web Shell, and AdaptixC2 via CVE-2026-82078 and CVE-2026-81578
results.description: On August 31, 2026, threat actors exploited two zero-day vulnerabilities in PaperCut MF affecting a customer in the Education sector. The attackers targeted an internet-facing print server running vulnerable PaperCut MF version 24.0.2, deploying an in-memory Java loader that established a web shell. Through this web shell, they delivered a trojanized Microsoft Copilot binary containing an AdaptixC2 implant. The implant connected to command-and-control infrastructure hosted on Alibaba servers. After remaining dormant for approximately one day, attackers returned to perform reconnaissance and Active Directory enumeration. They then stole a token from a domain-privileged service account and moved laterally to a domain controller. On the compromised domain controller, they dumped credentials from memory and registry, enabled Windows Restricted Admin mode for pass-the-hash attacks, and extracted the NTDS.dit database containing password hashes for all domain accounts, achieving complete domain compromise.

results.name: Swarming Against Citrix 0-Day Exploitation
results.description: A malicious cyber actor exploited a Citrix NetScaler Gateway zero-day vulnerability on September 24, 2026, three days before public disclosure. The attacker, using IP address 149.104.78.141, attempted exploitation that was detected through behavioral analysis despite no CVE-specific signatures existing at the time. The exploitation chain aimed to establish persistence through a password-protected webshell, attempting to set setuid and setgid bits on /bin/sh for root access. The attacker tried to configure the web server to execute a hidden PHP webshell disguised as a CSS file, using aliases to route requests. Though unsuccessful in compromising the targeted sensor, the post-exploitation playbook revealed sophisticated techniques for maintaining access and evading detection through web server manipulation.

results.name: Star Blizzard refines phishing and malware delivery with the RedFlick technique
results.description: Since January 2026, Microsoft has observed Russian state threat actor Star Blizzard evolve their detection evasion capabilities through large-scale phishing campaigns, the use of accounts on compromised websites, and a novel malware delivery technique that Microsoft tracks as “RedFlick”. These changes represent a notable shift in the actor’s operational tradecraft and support ongoing cyberespionage activity targeting Ukrainian individuals and institutions as well as international non-government organizations (NGOs), Western think tanks, governments, and other organizations associated with international policy—particularly those with a nexus in supporting Ukraine.

results.name: 2CLoader: A New Malware Loader Delivering Vidar and Remus
results.description: In August 2026, a new loader designated 2CLoader was identified being used to distribute information stealers including Vidar and Remus, along with XWorm RAT. The loader implements extensive anti-analysis capabilities including anti-VM, anti-debug, and user activity checks. It employs sophisticated evasion techniques such as indirect system calls using Hell's Gate technique and inline trampoline hooks to bypass endpoint security detection. The loader stores its configuration and encrypted payload as a PE resource, using rolling XOR and AES-GCM encryption for payload protection. It supports multiple payload execution methods including RunPE, LoadPE, and CLR hosting for .NET assemblies. Network communication with command-and-control servers uses HTTP POST requests with JSON formatted messages encrypted via XOR. Multiple persistence mechanisms are available through registry keys, scheduled tasks, and startup folders.

results.name: Unauthenticated command injection on internet-facing mail servers: tracking CVE-2026-73570
results.description: Microsoft Threat Intelligence identified active exploitation of CVE-2026-73570, an unauthenticated OS command injection vulnerability in Zimbra Collaboration Suite's SNMP notification path. Exploitation occurred between patch availability on July 20, 2026 and public disclosure on August 13, 2026. Attackers delivered JSP webshells and reverse shells without requiring authentication, achieving privilege escalation through PAM configuration abuse and establishing persistent access via systemd services. Post-exploitation activity included cluster-wide lateral movement using Zimbra SSH keys, collection of authentication secrets and mailbox data, and attempted exfiltration using cloud-storage tools. Multiple organizations across different regions and industries were affected through both automated payload delivery and hands-on-keyboard operations targeting internet-facing Zimbra mail servers.

results.name: Inside Coruna and DarkSword Chains: From Web Lures to iOS Exploitation
results.description: Seven months after initial disclosure, the Coruna iOS exploit framework continues to evolve, now deploying two distinct chains based on device operating system version. Targets running iOS 17.2.1 or earlier receive the legacy Coruna framework, while later builds receive DarkSword-derived chains. Analysis identified 608 domains delivering Coruna-family code, with 93 sites mapping to 21 distinct tracking collectors. Distribution spans dating portals, AI-companion platforms, cryptocurrency promotions, media streaming services, and compromised legitimate sites. The attack requires no user interaction beyond loading a webpage, operating through hidden iframes that deploy browser exploits leading to native code execution. Recovered modules include kernel memory manipulation, code-signing enforcement changes, process memory access, encrypted command-and-control communication, and cleanup routines. results.name: Kairos Hold'em: Dissecting a New Go-Based DDoS Botnet
results.description: Kairos is a newly documented DDoS botnet for Linux written in Go, designed to transform compromised machines into attack nodes. The bot establishes hundreds to thousands of TCP connections to operator-specified targets, maintaining them with minimal keepalive bytes every few seconds to exhaust victim services. Initial access occurs via Telnet using default root credentials with empty passwords. The payload is delivered through multi-fallback shell commands via HTTP from the same server used for command and control. The bot operates with a simple three-command protocol including hold, kill all, and kill unpause commands. It masquerades as a kernel worker thread and employs a build-per-C2 distribution model, with samples identified across multiple CPU architectures including x86_64, ARM, MIPS, and 386.

results.name: Trojanized Claude Code Extension Plants an SSH Backdoor
results.description: Version 2.1.313 of the Claude Code extension in the Cursor Marketplace was compromised on October 29th, 2026. A malicious 66-line loader was inserted before legitimate extension code in the extension.js file. Upon activation, it adds an attacker-controlled SSH key labeled 'svc-telemetry' to the victim's authorized_keys, attempts to enable local SSH services, and establishes a reverse SSH tunnel to 134.209.82.225. The implant collects reconnaissance data including hostname, user information, Git configuration, and environment variables containing credentials. It installs platform-specific persistence mechanisms using LaunchAgents on macOS, crontab on Linux, and scheduled tasks on Windows. Beacon data is transmitted unencrypted to the command-and-control infrastructure, providing persistent remote access through the established SSH tunnel.

results.name: Polymarket Breach Alert: Wallet-Draining Code Found in a Third-Party Script
results.description: A malicious JavaScript file was discovered in a third-party performance monitoring integration on Polymarket. The script, hosted on a DebugBear CDN URL, contained sophisticated code designed to access authenticated trading sessions, inspect user portfolios, and transfer cryptocurrency assets to attacker-controlled addresses. The payload searches for active trading clients and signers within the user's browser session, then attempts to sell positions or transfer tokens directly. Analysis revealed code that reads authentication context from local storage, traverses React component structures to locate trading functionality, and constructs EIP-712 signed messages to move assets. A fallback recipient address embedded in the script showed holdings exceeding $2.1 million. Production build metadata from Polymarket confirms removal of the DebugBear integration. While the script's malicious capabilities are established through static analysis, the total number of victims and aggregate losses remain unverified.
